fields.rationale: Bodies are grouped by the type of authority they represent: a board dedicated solely to one profession; a board spanning multiple technical/design professions; a board shared across medical or allied-health professions; a state public-health department; a general professional-licensing or regulation umbrella agency; or a labor, commerce, consumer-protection, or other general-government agency.

Boards are bucketed by the type of authority they represent: a board dedicated solely to one profession, a board shared across multiple related professions, a state health/public-health department, a broad professional licensing or regulation agency, a labor/commerce/consumer-protection department, or a state education department.

Rows are grouped by the functional type of the parent department—health, consumer protection, commerce, dedicated professional licensing, labor, secretary of state, education, or a residual catch-all—so the same real-world department type gets the same label regardless of which profession it oversees.

Values are grouped by the type of authority named as accreditor: a national body dedicated to that profession's programs, a regional or institutional higher-education accreditor, an explicit federal agency reference (USDE or CHEA), delegation to the licensing board's own discretion, a state-level agency or board, or an explicit combination of two or more distinct accreditor types.

Values are grouped by the dominant mechanism that unlocks reciprocal recognition: whether the state primarily requires equivalent standards, a minimum practice period, compact membership, passing a recognized exam or holding a national certificate, a simple endorsement with fee and good standing, mutual reciprocal agreement between the two states, a detailed multi-factor credential review, or only an emergency/temporary pathway.
